reason_scores.investor_reason: An outstanding business with outstanding management, bought to hold indefinitely.
reason_scores.agent_reason_matched: Recommends holding indefinitely; sell triggers say the default for a great business with able, honest managers is to hold indefinitely, and a rising price alone is not a reason to sell.

reason_scores.investor_reason: Concentration in a very few companies he understands well.
reason_scores.agent_reason_matched: Concentration is justified because the facts are simple and public: more than 90% of operating income comes from one simple concentrate business. The agent sizes the position at 25% of the portfolio.

reason_scores.investor_reason: The product's extraordinary consumer appeal and worldwide reach, which he had observed for decades.
reason_scores.agent_reason_matched: The most widely recognized trademark in the world, sold in more than 160 countries. Consumer preference is the moat, world share is rising, and per-capita consumption abroad leaves a long runway. The agent lacks the investor's decades of personal observation, which the packet could not supply.

reason_scores.investor_reason: Management (Goizueta and Keough, from 1981) refocused the company and executed; international sales accelerated.
reason_scores.agent_reason_matched: Management has run the company as a team since 1981 and reversed the entertainment diversification. World share rose from under 38% to nearly 45%, international per-capita consumption has a long runway, and about 76–79% of operating income comes from abroad.

reason_scores.investor_reason: A CEO combining marketing and financial skill, so product growth turns into shareholder returns.
reason_scores.agent_reason_matched: Management allocates capital for owners: about $5.20 of market value was created per $1 retained since 1981, 69M shares were bought back below value, and the share count is falling. The agent also cites pricing power and rising share.

notes: The agent matches the BUY decision and a concentrated size (25% against about 17–21%). Its main thesis is the investor's: a wonderful, understandable global franchise, refocused since 1981 by owner-minded management, held indefinitely. The biggest gap is emphasis. The agent leans on a detailed DCF and margin-of-safety calculation, while the investor's documented reasoning rests on qualitative judgment: decades of watching the product and personal knowledge of Goizueta and Keough. The agent says it recognizes the company but does not name it, and it relies only on pre-cutoff packet documents, so no leakage is flagged.
